title: Prediction of the Higgs Mass from a Quantum Field Theory with a Specific Lorentz-Violating Model
content: In our previous work, we proposed a specific Lorentz-violating model, whose most distinctive feature is that the momentum of a moving particle possesses an intrinsic cutoff proportional to the particle's rest mass. Building upon this Lorentz-violating model and simultaneously introducing the assumption of ultraviolet scale invariance, we find that, once this cutoff is incorporated into the Standard Model, electroweak symmetry breaking can be spontaneously induced by radiative corrections. Employing the complete two-loop renormalization group equations and an exact pole-mass conversion, we obtain a theoretical prediction for the Higgs boson pole mass of Mh = 125.08 GeV, which agrees with the experimental value of 125.11 ± 0.11 GeV within 1σ, thereby reducing the number of free parameters in the electroweak sector from two to one. Furthermore, we find that this mechanism can eliminate quadratic divergences at the kinematic level, which substantially alleviates the hierarchy problem in the Standard Model.
